fatal_errors: The proposed ZrC addition does not reconstruct the target intervention: optimized low-temperature HVAF-i7 deposition of FeCoNiCrAl.
The cited evidence concerns CrMnFeCoNi coatings on steel tested for aqueous NaCl corrosion and hardness, not oxidation or thermal-barrier bond-coat durability at 1000–1150 °C.
The proposed mechanism does not address the controlling target phenomena: coating porosity, deposition-stage oxidation, oxygen ingress, alumina TGO formation, interdiffusion, or scale spallation.
No quantitative temperature, exposure time, ZrC loading, coating architecture, or thermal-cycling/isothermal boundary is specified.

The falsification experiment measures corrosion and hardness rather than oxidation kinetics, TGO composition and thickness, internal oxidation, adhesion, or spallation, so it cannot establish improved TBC durability.
explanation: The hypothesis is broadly relevant to modifying an HEA coating and provides an untreated comparator, but it has little scientific agreement with the hidden target. Its evidence supports ZrC-induced hardness and aqueous corrosion changes in a different HEA/substrate/process system and cannot justify high-temperature bond-coat reliability. The predicted benefit is generic and unquantified, while the experiment lacks defined high-temperature conditions and durability-relevant measurements. A valid test would compare otherwise identical ZrC-containing and ZrC-free bond coats under specified oxidation or thermal-cycling conditions and quantify mass gain, alumina-TGO growth, internal oxidation, adhesion, cracking, and spallation.
